builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Titan-Llama: Retrofitting Pre-trained LLMs with External Neural Memory Modules
summary: The method replaces full attention over distant tokens with recurrent fixed-size neural memory modules updated at test time, while retaining full-fidelity attention over a recent block via a blockwise attention mask. It requires a post-training retrofit phase rather than pretraining from scratch, adds test-time parameter updates that increase implementation and serving complexity, and was validated only on a 1B model with medium context lengths. Failure modes include loss of precise recall of distant details compressed into the memory modules, sensitivity to block size and memory capacity, and uncertain transfer of the gains to larger models or very long contexts.
rationale: The approach is open-source and demonstrated on a 1B model, making it feasible on a single 24 GB GPU, but its test-time training machinery and single-model validation require workload-specific evaluation before production adoption.
technique: Test-time neural memory modules for long-context inference

It requires a post-training retrofit phase rather than pretraining from scratch, adds test-time parameter updates that increase implementation and serving complexity, and was validated only on a 1B model with medium context lengths. Failure modes include loss of precise recall of distant details compressed into the memory modules, sensitivity to block size and memory capacity, and uncertain transfer of the gains to larger models or very long contexts.

On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, over 20% faster prefill, 37% faster decode at medium context lengths, and 24% lower steady-state decode memory; accuracy on segmented windows rises from 23.87% to 40.51% on QuALITY and 14.50% to 40.75% on LongHealth.
